title: Complete Binary Tree Inserter
spaceBreakdown:
- queue<TreeNode*> candidates: up to n/2 + 1 entries (last-level nodes + possibly one partial parent) → O(n)
- queue<TreeNode*> q (constructor BFS): up to n/2 entries at widest level → O(n), freed after constructor
- TreeNode* root: O(1)
- not counted: input tree, returned root pointer
approach: Maintain a queue of "candidate" nodes - nodes in the complete binary tree that have at least one missing child, in level-order. On initialization, BFS the tree and collect all such nodes. On insert, the front of the queue is the next parent: if it lacks a left child, attach there (parent stays in queue since it still needs a right child); otherwise attach as right child and pop the parent (now complete). The new node always enters the queue. This guarantees O(1) per insert and keeps the tree complete.
hints: In a complete binary tree, which node receives the next inserted child? Walk the tree level by level, left to right - what property identifies the first node that is not yet "full"?
Use a queue of candidate parents (nodes missing at least one child). With tree [1, 2], node 1 is at the front with a missing right child, so insert(3) attaches 3 as 1's right child and returns 1.

```
constructor:
  BFS from root
  collect every node with < 2 children into a queue

insert(v):
  parent = front of queue
  if parent.left is empty:
    parent.left = new Node(v)
  else:
    parent.right = new Node(v)
    pop parent from queue
  push new Node(v) to queue
  return parent.val

get_root:
  return root
```

**Single node** - root has no children at all
`Input: [[1]], insert(2)` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: checking `parent->right` before `parent->left` → sets 2 as right child, tree becomes [1,null,2] instead of [1,2]

**Left insertion keeps parent** - parent still needs right child afterward
`Input: [[1,2,3]], insert(4), insert(5)` → `Expected: 2, 2`
⚠️ Bug: popping parent after left-child insertion → insert(5) returns 3 instead of 2

**Right insertion must pop** - parent is now complete
`Input: [[1,2]], insert(3), insert(4)` → `Expected: 1, 2`
⚠️ Bug: not popping parent after right-child insertion → insert(4) overwrites node 1's right child and returns 1 instead of 2

followUps.q: What if the tree can have up to 10^9 nodes - can you still support O(1) insert without storing all candidates?
followUps.a: Track the total node count. To find the insertion parent, write the count in binary, drop the leading 1, then walk from the root using each remaining bit (0 = left, 1 = right). This gives O(log n) per insert and O(1) auxiliary space.

followUps.q: What if you also need to support deleting the most recently inserted node?
followUps.a: Decrement the node count and use the same binary-navigation trick to reach the last node, then detach it from its parent. Each delete is O(log n); the tree stays complete because you always remove the rightmost last-level node.

followUps.q: What if the tree is stored as an array (heap-style indexing) instead of linked nodes?
followUps.a: Insert is just appending to the array - the parent of the new node at index n is at index (n−1)/2. No queue is needed; both insert and get_root are O(1) with O(1) auxiliary space beyond the array itself.
